```ts
persistor.object(settings).path({ storageKey: 'app', path: ['settings'] });

// Persist each record separately (good for large collections)
persistor.collection(users).records({ bucketName: 'users' }); // memory/indexedDb only

await persistor.hydrate(); // load from storage into collections
persistor.start();          // autosave on every queue.flush()
```

### Delta writes (persist only changed keys)

Default: any change writes the WHOLE snapshot (`takeSnapshot()` reads the whole
collection; `strategy.write` rewrites all of it) — `O(N)` per flush. A strategy can
opt into key-granular writes by implementing the optional
`writeDelta(persistor, delta)`. When it does AND the source is key-aware (an
`OIMReactiveCollection`, whose `subscribeOnAnyUpdate` reports changed PKs), the
engine sends only what changed in the flush instead of the full snapshot:

```ts
import { TOIMPersistDelta } from '@oimdb/persist';
// delta: { upserts: Array<{ key, value }>; deletedKeys: key[] }
async writeDelta(p, delta: TOIMPersistDelta<string, User>) {
    for (const { key, value } of delta.upserts) p.storage.put(key, value);
    for (const key of delta.deletedKeys) p.storage.delete(key);
}
```

- Opt-in and optional. A whole-blob backend (one localStorage key, one KV entry) OMITS
  `writeDelta` → engine always full-rewrites (a single-key change still rewrites the
  whole collection — by design / unavoidable there).
- A `writeDelta` strategy owns its per-key storage format; the resource-level
  whole-snapshot `codec` is NOT applied on the delta path.
- Manual `persist()` always writes full snapshots; deltas apply to the autosave path
  (`start()` + change + `flush`), where the changed keys are known.
- `collection.clear()` enumerates every removed key in its UPDATE / `subscribeOnAnyUpdate`
  payload — it is NOT an empty-`pks` "reset" signal. So the delta path deletes the cleared
  rows (they arrive as `deletedKeys`), snapshot-manager records them as deletions, and
  keyed subscribers on any cleared key are notified. Clearing an empty collection emits
  nothing. Same for `OIMObject.clear()` (enumerates removed keys).
- Built-in: the `records` strategies of `-memory` and `-idb` implement `writeDelta`
  (IndexedDB batches changed rows into the shared tx instead of clearing+rewriting the
  table). `entry`/`path` (localStorage, async-kv) do not.
- Exported types: `TOIMPersistDelta`, `TOIMPersistKeyedCapability` (source side),
  `TOIMPersistBatchItem` (for backends overriding `batchPersist`).

### Error handling

```ts
const persistor = createLocalStoragePersistor({
    onError: (error, { resource, operation }) => {
        console.error(`Persist ${operation} failed`, error);
    },
});
```

### Schema versioning / migration

```ts
import { createVersionedCodec } from '@oimdb/persist';

const codec = createVersionedCodec({
    version: 2,
    migrations: {
        1: (data) => ({ ...data, newField: 'default' }), // v0 → v1
        2: (data) => renameField(data),                   // v1 → v2
    },
});

persistor.collection(users).entry({ storageKey: 'users', codec });
```

## Devtools (`@oimdb/devtools`)

Register collections and computeds by name. Keep registration in separate `*.debug.ts` files — excluded from production.

```ts
// src/store/users.debug.ts
import { registry } from '@oimdb/devtools';
import { usersCollection, byRole } from './users';

registry.collection('users', usersCollection, {
    indexes: { byRole },
});
```

```ts
// src/store/tasks.debug.ts
import { registry } from '@oimdb/devtools';
import { tasksCollection, byAssignee, openTaskCount } from './tasks';

registry
    .collection('tasks', tasksCollection, {
        indexes: { byAssignee },
        relations: { assigneeId: 'users' }, // FK: tasks.assigneeId → users
    })
    .computed('openTaskCount', openTaskCount);
```

```ts
// src/debug.ts — single debug entry point
import './store/users.debug';
import './store/tasks.debug';

import { registry } from '@oimdb/devtools';
if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
    (window as Record<string, unknown>).__OIMDB_DEV__ = registry;
}
```

```ts
registry.dump(); // prints full state summary to console
registry.inspect(); // returns structured JSON
```

When a computed dep's source is not registered, it shows as `(unregistered)` in `dump()` — a signal to go add it to the debug file.

Install the browser extension from `packages/browser-extension/` (load unpacked in Chrome) for a live DevTools panel.

## Naming Conventions

| Kind | Prefix | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Class | `OIM` | `OIMCollection` |
| Interface | `IOIM` | `IOIMCollectionStore` |
| Type | `TOIM` | `TOIMCollectionOptions` |
| Enum | `EOIM` | `EOIMCollectionEventType` |

Variable names: drop the prefix, start lowercase. Context goes first: `prevCollectionIndexFactory`, not `collectionIndexFactoryPrev`.

## File Conventions

- One file → one named export
- Filename matches export name exactly
- Types → `src/types/`, Interfaces → `src/interfaces/`, Abstract classes → `src/abstract/`

## Common Patterns

### Wire up a complete feature

```ts
const queue = new OIMEventQueue({ scheduler: new OIMEventQueueSchedulerImmediate() });

const { collection: tasks, indexFactory, select } =
    createOIMCollectionKit<Task, string>(queue, { selectPk: (t) => t.id });

const byStatus  = indexFactory.derivedSetIndex((t) => [t.status]);
const byAssignee = indexFactory.derivedSetIndex((t) => [t.assigneeId]);

const runtime = new OIMComputeRuntime(queue);

const openCount = new OIMComputed<number>(runtime, {
    compute: () => byStatus.getPksByKey('open').size,
    deps: [new OIMEffectDependencyKeyedIndex(byStatus, 'open')],
});
```

### Subscribe to a collection index

```ts
const unsubscribe = byStatus.subscribeOnKey('open', () => {
    console.log('open tasks:', byStatus.getPksByKey('open'));
});
// ...later
unsubscribe();
```

### Destroy lifecycle (always call destroy in reverse order)

Teardown is LIFO: dispose dependents before what they depend on — indexes / streams / selectors before the collection, the collection before the queue. By hand:

```ts
logEffect.destroy();
openCount.destroy();
byStatus.destroy();
tasks.destroy();
queue.destroy();
```

**`OIMDisposeScope`** does this for you — register as you build, tear everything down in one LIFO call. It accepts both `{ destroy(): void }` objects AND bare `() => void` unsubscribe functions (selectors' `watch`, per-key `subscribeOnKey`, `emitter.on`, scheduler tasks expose only the function form). `add(x)` returns `x` for inline capture; idempotent; every item is disposed even if one throws (first error rethrown after); `child()` nests a sub-scope. `createOIMDisposeScope()` factory. New exports: `OIMDisposeScope`, `createOIMDisposeScope`, `IOIMDisposable` (`{ destroy(): void }`), `TOIMDisposable` (`IOIMDisposable | (() => void)`).

```ts
const scope = new OIMDisposeScope();
const queue = scope.add(new OIMEventQueue());
const tasks = scope.add(new OIMReactiveCollection(queue, { selectPk: t => t.id }));
const byStatus = scope.add(tasks.indexFactory.setBasedIndex());
scope.add(select.entitiesBySetIndexKey(byStatus, 'open').watch(render));
// …later — one call, correct LIFO order, no manual bookkeeping:
scope.destroy();
```

## DevTools UI (`@oimdb/mcp devtools`)

For human developers — runs a local web UI at `http://localhost:7433`:

```bash
npx @oimdb/mcp devtools
```

Auto-opens in the browser. Shows live collections, computeds, and dep status from the running app. Requires `registry.connect()` in `debug.ts`.

## MCP Setup (`@oimdb/mcp`)

`@oimdb/mcp` lets AI assistants query live OIMDB state from the running browser tab.

### Check if MCP is already configured

Look for `mcpServers.oimdb` in `.claude/settings.json` (project) or `~/.claude/settings.json` (global). If present, call `oimdb_inspect` directly — no setup needed.

### Configure MCP (if not already done)

Add to the project MCP config and ask the user to reload their editor:

- Claude Code: `.claude/settings.json`
- Cursor: `.cursor/mcp.json`

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "oimdb": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@oimdb/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Connect the browser

The project's `debug.ts` (or `src/debug.ts`) must call `registry.connect()`:

```ts
import { registry } from '@oimdb/devtools';
registry.connect(); // ws://localhost:7432
```

If this line is missing, add it and ask the user to reload the page.

### Available tools

| Tool | Use it when |
|---|---|
| `oimdb_inspect` | Need full state — collections, computeds, deps |
| `oimdb_dump` | Need a quick readable summary |
| `oimdb_collection` | Debugging one specific collection |
| `oimdb_computed` | Debugging why a computed is stale or wrong |

### One-shot CDP (no MCP config needed)

If Chrome is running with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`:

```bash
npx @oimdb/mcp cdp
```

Prints full `inspect()` JSON to stdout. Use when MCP is not configured.


<!-- ========== packages/devtools/llms.txt ========== -->

# OIMDB

> **For AI assistants:** You are reading the OIMDB API reference. Read this file fully before writing any OIMDB code — the API has specific patterns that are easy to get wrong without context.
> After reading, look for `debug.ts` or `*.debug.ts` files in the project — they describe the specific data model (collections, indexes, relations, computeds) of the app you are working on.
> If `@oimdb/mcp` is in the project's MCP config, call `oimdb_inspect` for live runtime state from the browser.

OIMDB is a TypeScript in-memory reactive database. It stores entities in typed collections, maintains indexes, and propagates changes through a reactive graph (computed values, effects, selectors) controlled by an explicit event queue. All change delivery is batched: subscriptions fire on `queue.flush()`, never mid-mutation.

## Packages

| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `@oimdb/core` | Collections, indexes, event queue, reactive primitives |
| `@oimdb/persist` | Storage-agnostic persist/hydrate engine (source adapters, resources, versioned codec). Backends ship separately: `@oimdb/persist-memory`, `-localstorage`, `-idb`, `-async-kv`, `-json` |
| `@oimdb/react` | React hooks for collections and selectors |
| `@oimdb/exodra` | [Exodra](https://exodra.org) adapter: OIMDB selectors/computeds → read-only `TExoBindable` (no React) |
| `@oimdb/async` | Async-aware reactive collection and index variants |
| `@oimdb/devtools` | Debug registry: name collections/indexes/computeds, inspect runtime state |
| `@oimdb/snapshot-manager` | Snapshot/restore collection state |
| `@oimdb/redux-adapter` | Bridge OIMDB collections into a Redux store |

## Core Concepts

### Event Queue

All reactive updates are batched. Mutations accumulate, then `queue.flush()` delivers all changes at once.

```ts
import { OIMEventQueue, OIMEventQueueSchedulerImmediate } from '@oimdb/core';

const queue = new OIMEventQueue({
    scheduler: new OIMEventQueueSchedulerImmediate(), // macrotask: setImmediate (Node), fallback MessageChannel / setTimeout(0) (browser)
    onError: (e) => reportToSentry(e),                // optional; see below
});
// or: OIMEventQueueSchedulerMicrotask (next microtask, before paint — lowest latency),
//     OIMEventQueueSchedulerAnimationFrame, OIMEventQueueSchedulerTimeout
// Async schedulers coalesce; call queue.flush() directly for sync delivery (e.g. tests).
// OIMEventQueueSchedulerSync (createSync()) flushes synchronously per write, NO batching —
//   debug/diagnostic only: swap in at the root to test if a bug is coalescing-related.
```

**Errors during flush.** If a task (subscriber / effect / computed) throws while the queue is flushing, the other tasks in that flush still run (each is isolated) and the queue's internal state is always restored — one bad task never wedges the queue. By default the error is then **raised, not swallowed**: it propagates out of `flush()` (thrown to the caller of a manual flush, or uncaught in async/scheduled mode). Pass `onError` to handle it instead (then it is NOT re-raised). Regardless of `onError`, a `EOIMEventQueueEventType.FLUSH_ERROR` event (payload `TOIMFlushError = { error }`) is emitted per failing task — the channel `@oimdb/devtools` `trackFlushErrors` / MCP use to surface failed flushes.

### Collections

`OIMCollection` — base CRUD store. `OIMReactiveCollection` — same + emits events on flush.

```ts
import { OIMReactiveCollection } from '@oimdb/core';

interface User { id: string; name: string; role: 'admin' | 'member'; }

const users = new OIMReactiveCollection<User, string>(queue, {
    selectPk: (u) => u.id,
});

users.upsertMany([
    { id: 'u1', name: 'Alice', role: 'admin' },
    { id: 'u2', name: 'Bob',   role: 'member' },
]);
users.upsertOne({ id: 'u1', name: 'Alice Smith', role: 'admin' }); // update
users.removeOne({ id: 'u2', name: 'Bob', role: 'member' });

users.getOneByPk('u1');   // → entity or undefined
users.getAll();            // → TEntity[]
users.getAllPks();          // → TPk[]
```

### Indexes

Indexes map keys to sets or arrays of PKs. Two storage shapes:
- **Set-based** — unordered, deduped (`OIMIndexManualSetBased`, `OIMReactiveIndexManualSetBased`)
- **Array-based** — ordered, with duplicates (`OIMIndexManualArrayBased`, `OIMReactiveIndexManualArrayBased`)

```ts
import { OIMReactiveIndexManualSetBased } from '@oimdb/core';

const byRole = new OIMReactiveIndexManualSetBased<'admin' | 'member', string>(queue);

byRole.setSlots('admin', [users.getSlotByPk('u1')!]);
byRole.getPksByKey('admin'); // → Set { 'u1' }

byRole.subscribeOnKey('admin', () => {
    console.log('admin set changed');
});
queue.flush(); // delivers subscription
```

**`subscribeOnKeys(keys, handler)` delivery is coalesced per flush:** the handler fires at most ONCE per flush no matter how many of the subscribed keys changed in it (the callback gets no key, so per-key fan-out would be pure waste). This holds across all reactive primitives — sync (collection / index / object, via `OIMCarrierKeyedEmitter`) and the `@oimdb/async` nodes (via `OIMUpdateEventEmitterAsync`) alike. `subscribeOnKey` (single key) is unchanged. Handler identity is preserved, so `unsubscribeFromKeys(keys, handler)` still removes a `subscribeOnKeys` subscription — and releases the coalescing exactly like the returned unsubscribe closure does.

**Coalescing is scoped to the subscription, not to the handler.** It applies only to handlers registered through a multi-key `subscribeOnKeys`. If the same function holds several *independent* `subscribeOnKey` subscriptions, it still gets one delivery per changed key — an unrelated multi-key subscription elsewhere on the same collection/index never changes that.

Membership writes are incremental (touch only the changed pks):
- `addPks(key, pks)` / `removePks(key, pks)` — **set-based**: O(1) per pk for both. **array-based**: `addPks` O(1), `removePks` O(bucket) (ordered, must scan).
- For frequently changing membership (e.g. a **virtual/windowed list** indexing the on-screen rows, adding/removing on scroll) prefer **set-based**.
- `setPks` / `addPks` resolve each pk → slot (O(1) lookup); if you already hold slots (`collection.upsertMany` returns them) use `setSlots` / `appendSlots` to skip the lookup.
- `getEntitiesByKey(key)` returns `(TEntity | undefined)[]` — positional holes for not-yet-loaded pks, aligned with `getPksByKey` (not dropped), so you can render a loading state.

### Global (keyless / whole-collection) indexes

When you need ONE index/ordered list over the **whole collection** ("all") there is no meaningful key. Use a **Global** index instead of inventing a phantom key like `'all'`. Same two shapes (array-based ordered / set-based unordered) and two modes (manual / derived), but keyless: `getPks()` / `getSlots()` / `getEntities()` take no key, and `subscribe(handler)` replaces `subscribeOnKey`. Internally a Global index holds ONE bucket with a single-carrier emitter (no key→carrier map / hashing), so it is strictly cheaper than a keyed index with one key.

Classes mirror the keyed ones with `Global` inserted: `OIMGlobalIndexManual{Array,Set}Based` (raw slots), `OIMReactiveGlobalIndexManual{Array,Set}Based`, `OIMReactiveCollectionGlobalIndexManual{Array,Set}Based` (pk writes), `OIMDerivedCollectionGlobalIndex{Array,Set}Based`.

```ts
// Manual, collection-bound (pk writes) — e.g. a server-provided page order
const list = indexFactory.arrayBasedGlobalIndex();
list.setPks(['u2', 'u1']);          // also addPks / removePks (no key)
list.getPks();                       // ['u2', 'u1']
list.subscribe(() => { /* one bucket changed */ });
queue.flush();

// Derived — auto-tracks the whole collection, ordered
const recent = indexFactory.derivedArrayGlobalIndex({ orderBy: (u) => u.createdAt });
recent.getEntities();                // (User | undefined)[] in order, kept in sync

// Derived set — whole-collection membership; `filter` narrows it
const active = indexFactory.derivedSetGlobalIndex({ filter: (u) => !u.archived });
```

- Derived options: `orderBy` / `compareEntities` (array only) for order, `filter: (e) => boolean` to include a subset (default: entity exists), `buildInitial` (default true).
- Selectors: `select.entitiesByArrayGlobalIndex(list)` / `select.entitiesBySetGlobalIndex(set)` → `(TEntity | undefined)[]` (no key).
- React: `useSelectEntitiesByGlobalIndex{Array,Set}Based(collection, index)`, `useSelectPksByGlobalIndex{Array,Set}Based(index)`, plus `…Signal` variants — all drop the `key` argument.

### Composite (key-path) indexes

When the key is a **combination of values** (e.g. `[userId, projectId, role]`) rather than one primitive, use a **composite** set-based index instead of concatenating a string key. Create it with `indexFactory.compositeSetIndex()`. The key is a `TOIMKeyPath` — an ordered, **arbitrary-length** tuple of primitive segments (`readonly (string | number)[]`). Every method that takes a `key` takes a path array instead; everything else (pk writes, slot resolution, reactivity, `getEntitiesByKey` holes) is identical to `setBasedIndex`.

```ts
const membersByScope = indexFactory.compositeSetIndex();
membersByScope.setPks(['u1', 'p1', 'admin'], ['m1', 'm2']); // also addPks / removePks
membersByScope.getPksByKey(['u1', 'p1', 'admin']);          // Set { 'm1', 'm2' }
membersByScope.getEntitiesByKey(['u1', 'p1', 'admin']);     // (Member | undefined)[]
membersByScope.subscribeOnKey(['u1', 'p1', 'admin'], () => {/* … */});
queue.flush();
```

- **Matched by content, not reference / string.** A freshly built `['u1','p1','admin']` resolves to the same bucket as the one written earlier — no need to reuse the array instance. Segments keep their own type (`1` ≠ `'1'`) and no separator can collide (`['a|b','c']` ≠ `['a','b|c']`), unlike a `"a|b|c"` string key.
- **Full path is the lookup unit.** O(arity) — effectively O(1) for a fixed arity — a lookup walks one native-`Map` level per segment. No partial/prefix queries (subscribe/lookup are by the whole path). Paths of different lengths coexist (`['a','b']` and `['a','b','c']` never collide).
- **No perf cost to primitive indexes.** It is a distinct opt-in index: `setBasedIndex` and all others keep their native-`Map` fast path untouched. The trie cost is paid only where you use a composite index.
- **Ordered variant:** `indexFactory.compositeArrayIndex()` — same key path, but buckets are ordered slot arrays (`getPksByKey` returns an array in write order). Use it when order matters per composite key (e.g. `[channelId, threadId]` messages).
- **Selectors:** `select.entitiesByCompositeSetIndexKey(index, path)` / `select.entitiesByCompositeArrayIndexKey(index, path)` → `(TEntity | undefined)[]`, tracking both index and entity changes.
- **React:** `useSelectEntitiesByCompositeIndexKey{Set,Array}Based(collection, index, path)` and `useSelectPksByCompositeIndexKey{Set,Array}Based(index, path)`. Unlike the primitive hooks (which stabilize the key by `===`), these stabilize the path **by content**, so a freshly built `['p1','admin']` on every render does not re-subscribe.
- New exports: `OIMReactiveCollectionIndexCompositeTrie{Set,Array}Based`, `OIMIndexStoreTrieDriven{Set,Array}Based` (inject via `indexOptions.store` for a custom key path store), `OIMKeyPathCarrierProvider`, `OIMTrieMap` (the generic N-level trie util), types `TOIMKeyPath` / `TOIMKey`. The keyed-emitter / index generics accept `TKey extends TOIMKey` (= `TOIMPk | TOIMKeyPath`) — a pure widening; primitive keys are unaffected.

### Composite PRIMARY key (collection keyed by a tuple)

Beyond composite index *keys*, a **collection's PK itself** can be a composite path. Pass a trie store: `new OIMReactiveCollection(queue, { selectPk: e => [e.userId, e.projectId], store: new OIMCollectionStoreTrieDriven() })`. Then `getOneByPk([1,10])`, `subscribeOnKey([1,10])`, `removeOneByPk([1,10])` all match by content; the store interns each logical PK to one canonical `slot.pk` reference so downstream native `Set<pk>` stays correct. Primitive-PK collections keep `OIMCollectionStoreMapDriven` (native `Map`) untouched — no regression.

- **Indexes work over a composite-PK collection.** `indexFactory.setBasedIndex()` (or `compositeSetIndex`) on such a collection indexes composite PKs: `byRole.setPks('admin', [[1,10],[2,10]])`, `getPksByKey`, `addPks`, `removePks([[2,10]])` all match PKs by content (the per-bucket pk→slot membership uses the collection's trie key domain).
- **Serialization boundaries.** `@oimdb/persist` (stores entities as an array, re-derives the PK via `selectPk` on hydrate) and `@oimdb/snapshot-manager` (stores the PK as a value) round-trip a composite PK with **no codec** — just pass the composite-PK collection. **`@oimdb/redux-adapter`** keys Redux state by string (`Record<pk, entity>`), so a composite PK needs an `IOIMPkCodec`: pass it to `createCollectionReducer(collection, child?, mapper?, pkCodec)` — one codec drives both the default mapper (encode: `entities` keyed by JSON-encoded PK, `ids` keep the raw tuple) AND child write-back / linked-index sync (decode: Redux string key → raw PK). `OIMPkCodecKeyPath` is the ready codec. (Or pass `mapper: createDefaultCollectionMapper(codec)` directly for a read-only projection.)
- New exports: `OIMCollectionStoreTrieDriven`, `OIMKeyDomainTrie` / `OIMKeyDomainNative` (`IOIMKeyDomain`), `OIMTrieSet`, `IOIMPkCodec` / `OIMPkCodecKeyPath`. The collection/index PK generics accept `TPk extends TOIMKey`.

### Ordered list command stream

For an ordered per-key list that emits **position-addressed commands** (insert / remove / move / set / reset) instead of a new array to diff — for imperative renderers that apply edits in place. `OIMCollectionOrderedListCommandStream` (pk writes, via `indexFactory.orderedList()`) or `OIMOrderedListCommandStream` (slot writes). Commands are not in the event payload — subscribe, then pull synchronously.

```ts
import { createOIMOrderedListMappedCommandStream } from '@oimdb/core';

stream.push('main', 'u1');           // append by pk; also insertAt/setAt/removeAt/removeRange/moveRange/set
stream.subscribeCommands('main', () => {
    for (const cmd of stream.consumeCommands('main')) {
        // { type:'insert', index, item } | { type:'remove', index, count? }
        // | { type:'move', from, to, count? } | { type:'set', index, item }
        // | { type:'reset', items }   — item is the entity slot; entity is item.item
    }
});
stream.getEntitiesByKey('main'); // (TEntity | undefined)[] — holes preserved
```

`count` defaults to 1 (read `count ?? 1`). A whole-list change collapses to a single `reset`. Reads: `getPksByKey` / `getSlotsByKey` / `getEntitiesByKey`.

**Mapping the list to your own elements** — `createOIMOrderedListMappedCommandStream(source, create)` projects element-wise: the same commands with `item` replaced by `create(slot)`'s result (a DOM node, view model, …). `create` is a plain function (no options object). Identity is positional — a `move` reuses the **same** mapped instance (never recreated); `create` runs on insert/set/reset/initial build. No teardown callback: the leaving element IS the `remove`/`set`/`reset` command the consumer applies against its own mirror, so cleanup belongs there. It needs no queue (rides the source's batching) and is itself an `IOIMOrderedListCommandSource`, so it consumes like the raw stream and chains via `.map(create)`. New exports: `IOIMOrderedListCommandSource`, `OIMOrderedListMappedCommandStream`, `createOIMOrderedListMappedCommandStream`.

```ts
const nodes = createOIMOrderedListMappedCommandStream(stream, (slot) => engine.makeNode(slot.item));
nodes.subscribeCommands('main', () => {
    for (const cmd of nodes.consumeCommands('main')) {
        // cmd.item is your node; tear it down on remove/set/reset from your own mirror
    }
});
nodes.getItemsByKey('main'); // current mapped elements — initial render
```

> Content updates (entity fields changed) are not list commands — they arrive via the collection's per-pk subscription. The stream carries structure only.

**Deriving commands from an index** — the stream above is written imperatively. To instead get commands from an index whose order is maintained automatically (`derivedArrayIndex`, or any reactive array-based index replaced via `setPks`), use `createOIMOrderedListCommandStreamDiffDriven(queue, index, opts?)` / `OIMOrderedListCommandStreamDiffDriven`. On each per-key index change it diffs the previous order against the new one and emits the `insert`/`move`/`remove` that transforms it — identity by pk (a reorder is a `move` of the same slot, never a recreate), delivered on `AFTER_FLUSH`. An order-preserving change emits nothing. `opts.resetThreshold` (default `0` = always diff): below that fraction of shared pks it emits one `reset` instead of many edits. Output is an `IOIMOrderedListCommandSource`, so `createOIMOrderedListMappedCommandStream` composes on top to carry your own nodes. New exports: `OIMOrderedListCommandStreamDiffDriven`, `createOIMOrderedListCommandStreamDiffDriven`, `TOIMOrderedListDiffOptions`, `diffOrderedListByPk` (pure diff), `OIMOrderedListCommandBuffer` (shared abstract base of both streams).

```ts
const cardsByDeck = cards.indexFactory.derivedArrayIndex((c) => c.deckId, { orderBy: (c) => c.position });
const stream = createOIMOrderedListCommandStreamDiffDriven(queue, cardsByDeck);
stream.subscribeCommands('deck1', () => engine.apply(stream.consumeCommands('deck1'))); // insert/move/remove
```

**Mapping a plain index to stable objects** — for an ordinary set/array index (no commands), `createOIMIndexSlotMap(index, create)` / `OIMIndexSlotMap` memoizes `create(slot)` by slot identity (a `WeakMap`): the same slot returns the same object reference on every read, so `React.memo` / `Object.is` diffing works and view-models are reused. Same plain-function shape as the ordered mapper, no `destroy` (plain values, GC reclaims). `getByKey(key)` → mapped objects; `.map(create)` chains; `subscribeOnKey`/`subscribeOnKeys` passthrough to the index. For a keyless global index use `createOIMGlobalIndexSlotMap(index, create)` / `OIMGlobalIndexSlotMap` — same memo with `getAll()` and `subscribe()` instead of the keyed variants. New exports: `OIMIndexSlotMap`, `createOIMIndexSlotMap`, `IOIMIndexSlotSource`, `OIMGlobalIndexSlotMap`, `createOIMGlobalIndexSlotMap`, `IOIMGlobalIndexSlotSource`.

```ts
const usersByTeam = users.indexFactory.derivedSetIndex((u) => u.teamId);
const rows = createOIMIndexSlotMap(usersByTeam, (slot) => makeRow(slot.item));
rows.subscribeOnKey('team1', () => { for (const row of rows.getByKey('team1')) { /* stable per slot */ } });
```

### Derived collections

`OIMDerivedCollection(queue, source, derive, opts?)` is a reactive collection whose entities are derived **one-to-one** from a source collection — `derived[pk] = derive(source[pk], pk)`, keyed by the SOURCE pk — kept in sync (add / update / remove) automatically. It is itself a first-class `OIMReactiveCollection`, so it can be indexed, selected, and derived-from again (join → join); maintenance runs on the source's **synchronous** update channel, so a chain of derivations stays consistent within a flush (delivery to keyed subscribers is batched on flush as usual). It parallels `OIMDerivedCollectionIndex*` and needs no compute runtime.

```ts
const nameView = new OIMDerivedCollection(queue, users,
    (u) => ({ id: u.id, full: `${u.first} ${u.last}` }));
nameView.getOneByPk('u1'); // { id, full } — stays in sync with `users`
```

- `opts.compare` (default `Object.is`) — skip a downstream update when a source change leaves the re-derived entity equal (pass a field/shallow compare to memoize finer; the default recomputes a fresh object each time, so it propagates every source change).
- `opts.store` — pass a trie-driven store when the source PK is composite (`TOIMKeyPath`).
- `opts.buildInitial` (default true).

### DX Layer — Collection Model

`createOIMCollectionKit` wires queue + collection + index factory + selectors together.

```ts
import { createOIMCollectionKit } from '@oimdb/core';

const { collection, indexFactory, select } =
    createOIMCollectionKit<User, string>(queue, { selectPk: (u) => u.id });

// Derived index: built automatically from entity data
const byRole = indexFactory.derivedSetIndex((u) => [u.role]);

// Reactive selectors
const adminUsers = select.entitiesBySetIndexKey(byRole, 'admin');
adminUsers.getValue();   // → (User | undefined)[]
adminUsers.watch((users) => { /* called on queue.flush() when value changes */ });

const u1 = select.byPk('u1');
u1.getValue(); // → User | undefined
```

The kit also fronts the compute system, so you don't hand-write dependency wrappers or manage a runtime. `on.*` builds dependencies; `kit.computed` / `kit.effect` create nodes on the queue's **shared** runtime (all computeds/effects/selectors on one queue form ONE dependency graph — so a computed can depend on selectors and on other collections) and register them in `kit.scope` for teardown:

```ts
const { collection, computed, effect, on } =
    createOIMCollectionKit<User, string>(queue, { selectPk: (u) => u.id });

const isAdmin = computed(
    [on.collection(collection, 'u1'), on.index(byRole, 'admin'), on.computed(orderCount)],
    () => collection.getOneByPk('u1')?.role === 'admin',
);
effect([on.computed(isAdmin)], () => console.log(isAdmin.get()));
```

`on` builders: `on.collection(collection, pk)`, `on.index(index, key)`, `on.object(object, key)`, `on.computed(computed)`. Need the runtime directly (e.g. outside a kit)? `getOIMComputeRuntime(queue)` returns the one shared runtime for a queue. The low-level primitives below are what these wrap.

**Runtime registry.** Every computed / effect / selector on a queue MUST share one runtime — they form one dependency graph, and topological levels only mean anything within a single runtime. Three functions manage that, all keyed by queue (there is no global instance; two queues get two runtimes, so tests need no reset):

| Function | Use |
|---|---|
| `getOIMComputeRuntime(queue)` | The runtime for a queue, created on first use. A destroyed one is replaced, never handed back. |
| `peekOIMComputeRuntime(queue)` | The runtime **if one exists**, else `undefined` — never creates. For devtools/teardown/assertions that must not change what they observe. A destroyed runtime reads as `undefined`. |
| `setOIMComputeRuntime(queue, runtime)` | Install your own (instrumented subclass, test double). Throws if `runtime.queue !== queue`. Call BEFORE anything builds the graph — nodes capture their runtime at construction, so a late swap splits the graph in two. Does not destroy the previous runtime. |

`runtime.destroy()` detaches it from the queue's `AFTER_FLUSH` and drops everything pending; `runtime.isDestroyed` reports it. Destroy the nodes first, then the runtime — destroying the runtime does not destroy the computeds/effects scheduled on it. Idempotent. Without it the subscription lives as long as the queue, which is harmless (the handler early-returns) but cannot be unwound.

### Computed Values

Derived values that recompute lazily when dependencies change. Recomputation is scheduled on `queue.flush()`.

```ts
import { OIMComputeRuntime, OIMComputed, OIMEffectDependencyKeyedCollection } from '@oimdb/core';

const runtime = new OIMComputeRuntime(queue);

const adminCount = new OIMComputed<number>(runtime, {
    compute: () => byRole.getPksByKey('admin').size,
    deps: [new OIMEffectDependencyKeyedCollection(users, /* pk */ 'u1')],
});

adminCount.get();        // → number (triggers recompute if dirty)
adminCount.getIfReady(); // → number | undefined (no recompute)
adminCount.isReady;      // → boolean
adminCount.needsRecompute; // → boolean
```

### Effects

Side effects that run when dependencies change, on `queue.flush()`.

```ts
import { OIMEffect, OIMEffectDependencyComputed } from '@oimdb/core';

const logEffect = new OIMEffect(runtime, {
    deps: [new OIMEffectDependencyComputed(adminCount)],
    run: () => {
        console.log('admin count:', adminCount.get());
    },
});
```

**Dependency types:**
- `OIMEffectDependencyKeyedCollection(collection, pk)` — watch a specific PK
- `OIMEffectDependencyKeyedObject(object, key)` — watch a key in a reactive object
- `OIMEffectDependencyKeyedIndex(index, key)` — watch a key in an index
- `OIMEffectDependencyComputed(computed)` — depend on another computed

Each keyed dependency watches exactly **one** key — the key argument is the whole key, so a composite key/PK path `[a, b]` is one key (never split into `a`, `b`). For a composite-PK collection or composite index, pass the tuple: `new OIMEffectDependencyKeyedCollection(reqs, ['t1', 'open'])`. To depend on several keys, add several dependencies to the effect's `deps` array.

### Objects

Key-value stores for singleton data (settings, flags, etc.).

```ts
import { OIMReactiveObject } from '@oimdb/core';

const settings = new OIMReactiveObject<'theme' | 'lang', string>(queue);
settings.setProperty('theme', 'dark');
settings.get('theme'); // → 'dark' | undefined
settings.getAll();     // → { theme: 'dark' }
```

## React (`@oimdb/react`)

```bash
npm install @oimdb/react
```

All hooks use `useSyncExternalStore` and re-render only when watched data changes.

```ts
import {
    OIMCollectionsProvider,
    useOIMCollectionsContext,
    useSelectEntityByPk,
    useSelectEntitiesByPks,
    useSelectEntitiesByIndexKeySetBased,
    useSelectEntitiesByIndexKeyArrayBased,
    useSelectPksByIndexKeySetBased,
    useSelectValueByObjectKey,
} from '@oimdb/react';
```

### Setup

```ts
// store.ts — outside React
const queue = new OIMEventQueue();
const { collection: users, indexFactory } =
    createOIMCollectionKit<User, string>(queue, { selectPk: (u) => u.id });
const byTeam = indexFactory.derivedSetIndex((u) => [u.teamId]);
export const collections = { users };

// App.tsx
<OIMCollectionsProvider collections={collections}>
    <App />
</OIMCollectionsProvider>

// Component.tsx
type AppCollections = typeof collections;
const { users } = useOIMCollectionsContext<AppCollections>();
```

### Hook reference

| Hook | What it watches |
|---|---|
| `useSelectEntityByPk(collection, pk)` | One entity by PK |
| `useSelectEntitiesByPks(collection, pks)` | Multiple entities by PKs |
| `useSelectEntitiesByIndexKeySetBased(collection, index, key)` | Entities via set index key |
| `useSelectEntitiesByIndexKeysSetBased(collection, index, keys)` | Entities via multiple set index keys |
| `useSelectEntitiesByIndexKeyArrayBased(collection, index, key)` | Entities via array index key (ordered) |
| `useSelectEntitiesByIndexKeysArrayBased(collection, index, keys)` | Entities via multiple array index keys |
| `useSelectPksByIndexKeySetBased(index, key)` | Just PKs from set index (no collection needed) |
| `useSelectPksByIndexKeyArrayBased(index, key)` | Just PKs from array index |
| `useSelectValueByObjectKey(object, key)` | One key from `OIMReactiveObject` |
| `useSelectValuesByObjectKeys(object, keys)` | Multiple keys from `OIMReactiveObject` |

All hooks above use `useSyncExternalStore` (Concurrent-safe; detect change by `Object.is` reference).

### Mutable mode + signal hooks (advanced, opt-in)

For update-heavy / fine-grained UIs, run a collection **in place** (no per-update object copy) and bind with the lighter **signal hooks** (re-render on the keyed notification, no `useSyncExternalStore`, no `Object.is`):

```ts
import { OIMReactiveCollection, createInPlaceEntityUpdater } from '@oimdb/core';
import { useSelectEntityByPkSignal, useSelectPksByIndexKeyArrayBasedSignal } from '@oimdb/react';

const cards = new OIMReactiveCollection(queue, {
    selectPk: c => c.id,
    updateEntity: createInPlaceEntityUpdater(), // mutate in place, no allocation
});
const card = useSelectEntityByPkSignal(cards, id); // sees in-place mutations (uSES would miss them)
```

Signal hooks: `useSelectEntityByPkSignal(collection, pk)`, `useSelectPksByIndexKeyArrayBasedSignal(index, key)`, `useSelectPksByIndexKeySetBasedSignal(index, key)`. Use the fine-grained pattern (parent reads pks by index key; each row reads its own entity by pk).

Trade-offs (use only when every reader is subscription-driven): NOT Concurrent-safe; the entity reference is stable across changes, so `React.memo` on entities, prev/next diffing, time-travel, and the default uSES hooks on the same collection won't see updates. Default to the standard immutable hooks; reach for this only when a profile shows the data layer is the bottleneck.

## Exodra (`@oimdb/exodra`)

```bash
npm install @oimdb/exodra @oimdb/core
```

The Exodra counterpart of `@oimdb/react`: instead of a hook + re-render, every OIMDB read becomes a read-only Exodra bindable (`TExoBindable<T> = { getValue(): T; subscribe(update): () => void }`). No React. Built on `@oimdb/core`'s `OIMSelector` (`{ getValue, watch }`) — the fine-grained subscription already lives there, so this is a thin adapter. Depends only on the type-only `@exodra/reactivity-types` (never the reactivity runtime); peer dep `@oimdb/core`. Everything produced is read-only, lazy + ref-counted (upstream subscribed only while a downstream subscriber exists → O(visible)) and SSR-safe (`getValue()` reads through, valid with no subscription — a reactive key resolves on every read, never stale).

```ts
import { exoDb } from '@oimdb/exodra';
import { bindable, derive, h } from '@exodra/reactivity';

const byTeam        = usersKit.indexFactory.derivedSetIndex<string>(u => u.teamId);
const byTeamOrdered = usersKit.indexFactory.derivedArrayIndex<string>(u => u.teamId, { orderBy: u => u.name });
const online        = usersKit.indexFactory.derivedSetGlobalIndex({ filter: u => u.online });

const db = exoDb({
    users: { kit: usersKit, indexes: { byTeam, byTeamOrdered, online } },
    tags:  { kit: tagsKit },                                 // no indexes → byPk / byPks only
});

const team = bindable('t1');
db.users.byPk('u1');                            // TExoBindable<User | undefined>
db.users.byTeam(team);                          // set index — the kind is inferred from the index
db.users.online();                              // global index — no key, and none is asked for
db.users.byTeamOrdered.rows(team, render);      // → bindables.children      (identity-stable)
db.users.byTeamOrdered.list('t1', render);      // → bindableLists.children  (O(delta), fixed key)
```

| Export | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `exoDb(spec)` | whole system at once: `{ name: { kit, indexes? } }` → record of typed views |
| `exoCollection(kit, indexes?)` | one collection's Exodra view; `kit` stays reachable for writes |
| `exoSource(read, subscribe)` | base primitive: a raw pair → a lazy, ref-counted bindable |
| `exoSelector(selector)` / `exoComputed(computed)` | an `OIMSelector` / `OIMComputed` → a bindable |
| `exoKeyed(keyBindable, makeSelector)` | a MOVING key: repoints the selector as the key changes |
| `exoCombine(sources, fn)` | multi-source derive (Exodra's own `derive` is single-source) |
| `exoChildren(source, { key, render })` | identity-stable children for any items |
| `exoList(stream, key, render)` | OIMDB ordered command stream → Exodra `bindableList` (commands map 1:1 to `TExoListOp`) |

Each named index becomes a CALLABLE member of that name carrying `pks`, `rows`, `subscribe` (and `list` on ordered ones), so the caller never picks a method to match the index kind and never passes the index object again. Any key accepts `TKey | TOIMExodraReadable<TKey>`. Dispatch is structural: array-based `getPksByKey` returns `TPk[]`, set-based returns `Set<TPk>`, keyless ones have none; composite indexes are the same classes with an array key, resolved per call via `Array.isArray(key)`. **`list` exists only on array-based indexes** — a stream is derived by diffing an order and a set has none; enforced in the types, and it builds/memoizes the stream itself. `indexes` is a second argument because a kit does not own its indexes (`kit.indexFactory` creates them, the app keeps them); if core ever lets a kit hold named indexes this becomes optional without a break.

**No function in this package takes an equality option, and there is no options type.** Equality belongs to whoever owns the value: `OIMSelector.areEqual` for selectors (override it), `OIMComputed`'s `compare` for computeds (pass at construction), your own `fn` for `exoCombine` (return a stable reference when content is unchanged), your own `subscribe` callback for `exoSource(read, subscribe)` (compare there and don't call `onChange` — that callback IS the extension point). Those owners run BELOW the bridge, so a filter here could only reject what they passed, never resurrect what they dropped; in-place entity updaters need no configuration anywhere. `exoCombine` drops recomputes landing on the same value, collapsing the N notifications N sources produce for one logical change — not glitch-free though, so put real fan-in in ONE `OIMComputed` forwarded via `exoComputed`. `exoChildren` reads are idempotent (same array reference back, no render, no eviction, until the key sequence changes) and require UNIQUE keys — a duplicate throws rather than placing one schema object twice. `exoList` memoizes `render` per item, so repeated `snapshot()` calls return the same row objects (identity is what Exodra reconciles on); the memo is pruned against the live order on snapshot and amortized past 2x the live row count. Multi-entity reads are length-aligned WITH HOLES, matching `@oimdb/react`. Pure aliases of a single core call (`getOneByPk`, `subscribeOnKey`, `getPksByKey`) are NOT exported — call core directly. Pair `exoDb` with Exodra's own DI: `createContextKey<typeof db>('db')`, created by the app since this package pulls types only. Exodra bucket bindings subscribe at *build* (not `onExoMount`); `<index>.subscribe(key, onChange)` covers `onExoMount`-scoped needs. No function takes more than one shape of argument: a fixed key and a moving key are different members (`<index>(key)` vs `<index>.for(keyBindable)`), never one member that inspects what it was given. `exoCombine`'s FIRST emit after subscribing always propagates — OIMDB sources fire synchronously on subscribe and a binding is built from `getValue()` then wired a moment later, so suppressing it leaves the region frozen at its build-time value. Sorting and filtering belong in the index (`derivedArrayIndex({ orderBy })`, or emit no key for excluded entities), not in `rows` — there they are maintained incrementally instead of recomputed per read. The PRIMITIVES are the load-bearing API: screens that sort/filter beyond an index, key rows off related data, or fan in across collections are built from `exoChildren` over an `OIMComputed` forwarded by `exoComputed`, and that is the intended path, not a fallback. Write-side is intentionally omitted (apps write via orchestration, e.g. cnstra, not from views).


## Persist (`@oimdb/persist`)

```ts
// Backends are separate packages: @oimdb/persist-localstorage / -idb / -memory / -async-kv / -json
import { createLocalStoragePersistor } from '@oimdb/persist-localstorage';

const persistor = createLocalStoragePersistor({});

// Persist entire collection as one key
persistor.collection(users).entry({ storageKey: 'app:users' });

// Persist at a nested path within one key
persistor.collection(users).path({ storageKey: 'app', path: ['collections', 'users'] });
persistor.object(settings).path({ storageKey: 'app', path: ['settings'] });

// Persist each record separately (good for large collections)
persistor.collection(users).records({ bucketName: 'users' }); // memory/indexedDb only

await persistor.hydrate(); // load from storage into collections
persistor.start();          // autosave on every queue.flush()
```

### Delta writes (persist only changed keys)

Default: any change writes the WHOLE snapshot (`takeSnapshot()` reads the whole
collection; `strategy.write` rewrites all of it) — `O(N)` per flush. A strategy can
opt into key-granular writes by implementing the optional
`writeDelta(persistor, delta)`. When it does AND the source is key-aware (an
`OIMReactiveCollection`, whose `subscribeOnAnyUpdate` reports changed PKs), the
engine sends only what changed in the flush instead of the full snapshot:

```ts
import { TOIMPersistDelta } from '@oimdb/persist';
// delta: { upserts: Array<{ key, value }>; deletedKeys: key[] }
async writeDelta(p, delta: TOIMPersistDelta<string, User>) {
    for (const { key, value } of delta.upserts) p.storage.put(key, value);
    for (const key of delta.deletedKeys) p.storage.delete(key);
}
```

- Opt-in and optional. A whole-blob backend (one localStorage key, one KV entry) OMITS
  `writeDelta` → engine always full-rewrites (a single-key change still rewrites the
  whole collection — by design / unavoidable there).
- A `writeDelta` strategy owns its per-key storage format; the resource-level
  whole-snapshot `codec` is NOT applied on the delta path.
- Manual `persist()` always writes full snapshots; deltas apply to the autosave path
  (`start()` + change + `flush`), where the changed keys are known.
- `collection.clear()` enumerates every removed key in its UPDATE / `subscribeOnAnyUpdate`
  payload — it is NOT an empty-`pks` "reset" signal. So the delta path deletes the cleared
  rows (they arrive as `deletedKeys`), snapshot-manager records them as deletions, and
  keyed subscribers on any cleared key are notified. Clearing an empty collection emits
  nothing. Same for `OIMObject.clear()` (enumerates removed keys).
- Built-in: the `records` strategies of `-memory` and `-idb` implement `writeDelta`
  (IndexedDB batches changed rows into the shared tx instead of clearing+rewriting the
  table). `entry`/`path` (localStorage, async-kv) do not.
- Exported types: `TOIMPersistDelta`, `TOIMPersistKeyedCapability` (source side),
  `TOIMPersistBatchItem` (for backends overriding `batchPersist`).

### Error handling

```ts
const persistor = createLocalStoragePersistor({
    onError: (error, { resource, operation }) => {
        console.error(`Persist ${operation} failed`, error);
    },
});
```

### Schema versioning / migration

```ts
import { createVersionedCodec } from '@oimdb/persist';

const codec = createVersionedCodec({
    version: 2,
    migrations: {
        1: (data) => ({ ...data, newField: 'default' }), // v0 → v1
        2: (data) => renameField(data),                   // v1 → v2
    },
});

persistor.collection(users).entry({ storageKey: 'users', codec });
```

## Devtools (`@oimdb/devtools`)

Register collections and computeds by name. Keep registration in separate `*.debug.ts` files — excluded from production.

```ts
// src/store/users.debug.ts
import { registry } from '@oimdb/devtools';
import { usersCollection, byRole } from './users';

registry.collection('users', usersCollection, {
    indexes: { byRole },
});
```

```ts
// src/store/tasks.debug.ts
import { registry } from '@oimdb/devtools';
import { tasksCollection, byAssignee, openTaskCount } from './tasks';

registry
    .collection('tasks', tasksCollection, {
        indexes: { byAssignee },
        relations: { assigneeId: 'users' }, // FK: tasks.assigneeId → users
    })
    .computed('openTaskCount', openTaskCount);
```

```ts
// src/debug.ts — single debug entry point
import './store/users.debug';
import './store/tasks.debug';

import { registry } from '@oimdb/devtools';
if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
    (window as Record<string, unknown>).__OIMDB_DEV__ = registry;
}
```

```ts
registry.dump(); // prints full state summary to console
registry.inspect(); // returns structured JSON
```

When a computed dep's source is not registered, it shows as `(unregistered)` in `dump()` — a signal to go add it to the debug file.

Install the browser extension from `packages/browser-extension/` (load unpacked in Chrome) for a live DevTools panel.

## Naming Conventions

| Kind | Prefix | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Class | `OIM` | `OIMCollection` |
| Interface | `IOIM` | `IOIMCollectionStore` |
| Type | `TOIM` | `TOIMCollectionOptions` |
| Enum | `EOIM` | `EOIMCollectionEventType` |

Variable names: drop the prefix, start lowercase. Context goes first: `prevCollectionIndexFactory`, not `collectionIndexFactoryPrev`.

## File Conventions

- One file → one named export
- Filename matches export name exactly
- Types → `src/types/`, Interfaces → `src/interfaces/`, Abstract classes → `src/abstract/`

## Common Patterns

### Wire up a complete feature

```ts
const queue = new OIMEventQueue({ scheduler: new OIMEventQueueSchedulerImmediate() });

const { collection: tasks, indexFactory, select } =
    createOIMCollectionKit<Task, string>(queue, { selectPk: (t) => t.id });

const byStatus  = indexFactory.derivedSetIndex((t) => [t.status]);
const byAssignee = indexFactory.derivedSetIndex((t) => [t.assigneeId]);

const runtime = new OIMComputeRuntime(queue);

const openCount = new OIMComputed<number>(runtime, {
    compute: () => byStatus.getPksByKey('open').size,
    deps: [new OIMEffectDependencyKeyedIndex(byStatus, 'open')],
});
```

### Subscribe to a collection index

```ts
const unsubscribe = byStatus.subscribeOnKey('open', () => {
    console.log('open tasks:', byStatus.getPksByKey('open'));
});
// ...later
unsubscribe();
```

### Destroy lifecycle (always call destroy in reverse order)

Teardown is LIFO: dispose dependents before what they depend on — indexes / streams / selectors before the collection, the collection before the queue. By hand:

```ts
logEffect.destroy();
openCount.destroy();
byStatus.destroy();
tasks.destroy();
queue.destroy();
```

**`OIMDisposeScope`** does this for you — register as you build, tear everything down in one LIFO call. It accepts both `{ destroy(): void }` objects AND bare `() => void` unsubscribe functions (selectors' `watch`, per-key `subscribeOnKey`, `emitter.on`, scheduler tasks expose only the function form). `add(x)` returns `x` for inline capture; idempotent; every item is disposed even if one throws (first error rethrown after); `child()` nests a sub-scope. `createOIMDisposeScope()` factory. New exports: `OIMDisposeScope`, `createOIMDisposeScope`, `IOIMDisposable` (`{ destroy(): void }`), `TOIMDisposable` (`IOIMDisposable | (() => void)`).

```ts
const scope = new OIMDisposeScope();
const queue = scope.add(new OIMEventQueue());
const tasks = scope.add(new OIMReactiveCollection(queue, { selectPk: t => t.id }));
const byStatus = scope.add(tasks.indexFactory.setBasedIndex());
scope.add(select.entitiesBySetIndexKey(byStatus, 'open').watch(render));
// …later — one call, correct LIFO order, no manual bookkeeping:
scope.destroy();
```

## DevTools UI (`@oimdb/mcp devtools`)

For human developers — runs a local web UI at `http://localhost:7433`:

```bash
npx @oimdb/mcp devtools
```

Auto-opens in the browser. Shows live collections, computeds, and dep status from the running app. Requires `registry.connect()` in `debug.ts`.

## MCP Setup (`@oimdb/mcp`)

`@oimdb/mcp` lets AI assistants query live OIMDB state from the running browser tab.

### Check if MCP is already configured

Look for `mcpServers.oimdb` in `.claude/settings.json` (project) or `~/.claude/settings.json` (global). If present, call `oimdb_inspect` directly — no setup needed.

### Configure MCP (if not already done)

Add to the project MCP config and ask the user to reload their editor:

- Claude Code: `.claude/settings.json`
- Cursor: `.cursor/mcp.json`

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "oimdb": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@oimdb/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Connect the browser

The project's `debug.ts` (or `src/debug.ts`) must call `registry.connect()`:

```ts
import { registry } from '@oimdb/devtools';
registry.connect(); // ws://localhost:7432
```

If this line is missing, add it and ask the user to reload the page.

### Available tools

| Tool | Use it when |
|---|---|
| `oimdb_inspect` | Need full state — collections, computeds, deps |
| `oimdb_dump` | Need a quick readable summary |
| `oimdb_collection` | Debugging one specific collection |
| `oimdb_computed` | Debugging why a computed is stale or wrong |

### One-shot CDP (no MCP config needed)

If Chrome is running with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`:

```bash
npx @oimdb/mcp cdp
```

Prints full `inspect()` JSON to stdout. Use when MCP is not configured.


<!-- ========== packages/exodra/llms.txt ========== -->

# @oimdb/exodra

> **For AI assistants:** Adapter from OIMDB to [Exodra](https://exodra.org) reactivity — the Exodra
> counterpart of `@oimdb/react`. Instead of a hook + re-render, every OIMDB read becomes a read-only
> Exodra bindable (`TExoBindable<T> = { getValue(): T; subscribe(update): () => void }`).
> Read `@oimdb/core`'s reference first — this package only adapts its selector layer. Depends on the
> type-only `@exodra/reactivity-types` (no reactivity runtime); peer dep `@oimdb/core`.

## Model

- OIMDB `OIMSelector<T>` is `{ getValue(), watch(onValue) }`; Exodra `TExoBindable<T>` is
  `{ getValue(), subscribe(update) }`. Same shape → this package is a thin adapter.
- Fine-grained subscription (index key for membership + each pk in the set, re-subscribing when the
  set changes) already lives in the `@oimdb/core` selectors. This package does NOT re-implement it.
- Everything produced is **read-only**, **lazy + ref-counted** (upstream subscribed only while a
  downstream subscriber exists → O(visible)) and **SSR-safe** (`getValue()` reads through, valid with
  no subscription; a reactive key is resolved on every read, never stale).
- Exodra buckets: `h(type, { static, bindables, bindableLists, handlers, bindableHandlers })`. Flat
  props are a compile error there. `rows` feeds `bindables.children`; `list` feeds `bindableLists`.
- **No equality options exist in this package, and no options type.** Equality belongs to the value's
  owner: `OIMSelector.areEqual`, `OIMComputed.compare`, your `fn` in `exoCombine` (return a stable
  reference), your `subscribe` callback in `exoSource(read, subscribe)`. Those run BELOW the bridge,
  so a filter here could only reject what they passed, never resurrect what they dropped. In-place
  entity updaters therefore need no configuration anywhere.

## The two doors

```ts
exoDb<TSpec>(spec: TSpec): TOIMExodraDbViews<TSpec>
exoCollection<TEntity, TPk, TIndexes>(kit: TOIMCollectionKit<TEntity, TPk>, indexes?: TIndexes): TOIMExodraCollection<TEntity, TPk, TIndexes>
```

```ts
const db = exoDb({
    users: { kit: usersKit, indexes: { byTeam, byTeamOrdered, online } },  
    tags:  { kit: tagsKit },                                // no indexes → byPk / byPks only
});
```

Fixed members: `kit` (escape hatch back to OIMDB — writes, effects, computeds), `byPk(pk)`,
`byPks(pks)`. Every named index becomes a member of that name.

`indexes` is a second argument because a kit does NOT own its indexes — `kit.indexFactory` creates
them and the app keeps them. If core ever lets a kit hold named indexes, this argument becomes
optional without a break.

## Index facade — the kind is inferred from the index

Each named index is a CALLABLE object carrying everything you can do with it, so the caller never
picks a method to match the index kind and never passes the index object again:

```ts
users.byTeam(key)                     // TExoBindable<readonly (TEntity | undefined)[]>
users.byTeam.pks(key)                 // TExoBindable<readonly TPk[]>
users.byTeam.rows(key, render)        // TExoBindable<readonly TSchema[]>  → bindables.children
users.byTeam.for(keyBindable)         // pin to a MOVING key → a facade taking no key at all
users.byTeamOrdered.list(key, render) // TExoBindableList<TSchema>         → bindableLists.children
users.byTeam.subscribe(key, onChange): () => void   // manual, onExoMount scope
```

`render` is `(entity: TExoBindable<TEntity | undefined>, pk: TPk) => TSchema` — each row gets its OWN
entity bindable, so a field edit updates in place (array unchanged → reconcile no-op, focus safe).

Every key argument EXCEPT `list`'s accepts `TKey | TOIMExodraReadable<TKey>`; a bindable key repoints
the subscription without recreating the view. `list` takes a plain key only — a `TExoBindableList` is
bound once and driven by ops, so following a moving key would mean resetting the whole list on every
change, which is what `rows` already does better. Passing a bindable there is a compile error. A **global** (keyless) index takes no key at all: `users.online()`,
`users.online.rows(render)`.

**`list` exists ONLY on array-based (ordered) indexes** — a command stream is derived by diffing an
order, and a set has none. Enforced in the types (`TOIMExodraIndexFacade`) and absent at runtime.
It builds and memoizes the diff-driven stream itself; do not construct one by hand.

Dispatch is STRUCTURAL, not by class: array-based `getPksByKey` returns `TPk[]`, set-based returns
`Set<TPk>`, keyless ones have no `getPksByKey`. Composite (key-path) indexes are the same classes with
an array key, so the composite selector is chosen per call from `Array.isArray(key)`.

## Primitives

One signature each. Nothing here inspects an argument to work out which call you meant — a fixed key
and a moving key are different functions, not one function that sniffs.

```ts
exoSource<T>(read: () => T, subscribe: (onChange: () => void) => () => void): TExoBindable<T>
exoSelector<T>(selector: OIMSelector<T>): TExoBindable<T>
exoComputed<T>(computed: OIMComputed<T>): TExoBindable<T>
exoKeyed<TKey, T>(key: TOIMExodraReadable<TKey>, makeSelector: (key: TKey) => OIMSelector<T>): TExoBindable<T>
exoCombine<T>(sources: readonly TOIMExodraReadable<unknown>[], fn: () => T): TExoBindable<T>
exoChildren<TItem, TSchema>(source: TExoBindable<readonly TItem[]>, opts: { key: (i: TItem) => TOIMKey; render: (i: TItem) => TSchema }): TExoBindable<readonly TSchema[]>
exoList<TKey, TItem, TSchema>(stream: IOIMOrderedListCommandSource<TKey, TItem>, key: TKey, render: (item: TItem) => TSchema): TExoBindableList<TSchema>
```

`exoSource` is the base; the others are built on it. `exoKeyed` always takes a BINDABLE key — a fixed
key is `exoSelector(makeSelector(key))`.

**The primitives are the load-bearing API.** The facade covers "one index → its rows". Screens that
sort or filter beyond an index, key rows off related data, or fan in across collections are built
from `exoChildren` over a computed source, and that is the intended path, not a fallback.

**Aggregation belongs in `OIMComputed`, forwarded with `exoComputed`.** Joins, counts and roll-ups go
in one computed (leveled at AFTER_FLUSH, coherent) whose value the view reads; `exoChildren` then
takes an arbitrary `key`, so a row key derived from related data is expressible there.

`exoCombine` is for ordinary multi-source view values (an entity plus its author, an entity plus
local UI state). **Its first emit after subscribing always propagates**: OIMDB sources fire
synchronously on subscribe and a binding is normally built from `getValue()` and wired a moment
later, so suppressing that emit as redundant leaves the region frozen at its build-time value. Later
emits are deduped; for content dedup return a stable reference from `fn`. It is not glitch-free — a
reason to keep heavy fan-in in one `OIMComputed`, NOT a reason to avoid it for two-source values.

`exoChildren` reads are idempotent: the key sequence is compared to the previous one, so repeated
`getValue()` returns the SAME array reference and never renders or evicts. Keys must be UNIQUE — a
duplicate throws (one schema object cannot occupy two positions under identity reconciliation).

`exoList` memoizes `render` per item, so a row keeps one schema while it stays in the list and
repeated `snapshot()` calls return the same objects. Slots are stable carriers (reorder = `move` of
the same object). The memo is pruned against the live order — exactly on `snapshot()`, amortized past
2× the live row count — so position-addressed `remove` needs no bookkeeping.

### Sorting and filtering belong in the index, not in `rows`

`rows` deliberately has no sort/filter hook. Both are expressible where they are maintained
incrementally instead of recomputed per read:

```ts
// ordered column: order lives in the index, and `.list` (O(delta)) becomes available too
kit.indexFactory.derivedArrayIndex(t => t.statusId, { orderBy: t => t.createdAt })
// filtered index: emit no key for what you want excluded
kit.indexFactory.derivedSetIndex(t => (t.archived ? [] : [t.statusId]))
```

## Types

`TOIMExodraCollection`, `TOIMExodraDbViews`, `TOIMExodraIndexFacade`, `TOIMExodraKeyedIndexFacade`,
`TOIMExodraOrderedIndexFacade`, `TOIMExodraGlobalIndexFacade`, `TOIMExodraKeyArg`,
`TOIMExodraReadable`.

Multi-entity reads are length-aligned WITH HOLES (`(TEntity | undefined)[]`), matching `@oimdb/react`.
Pair `exoDb` with Exodra's own DI: `createContextKey<typeof db>('db')` (created by the app — this
package pulls types only, never the runtime).
Write-side is intentionally omitted (apps write via orchestration, e.g. cnstra, not from views).


<!-- ========== packages/persist/llms.txt ========== -->

# OIMDB

> **For AI assistants:** You are reading the OIMDB API reference. Read this file fully before writing any OIMDB code — the API has specific patterns that are easy to get wrong without context.
> After reading, look for `debug.ts` or `*.debug.ts` files in the project — they describe the specific data model (collections, indexes, relations, computeds) of the app you are working on.
> If `@oimdb/mcp` is in the project's MCP config, call `oimdb_inspect` for live runtime state from the browser.

OIMDB is a TypeScript in-memory reactive database. It stores entities in typed collections, maintains indexes, and propagates changes through a reactive graph (computed values, effects, selectors) controlled by an explicit event queue. All change delivery is batched: subscriptions fire on `queue.flush()`, never mid-mutation.

## Packages

| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `@oimdb/core` | Collections, indexes, event queue, reactive primitives |
| `@oimdb/persist` | Storage-agnostic persist/hydrate engine (source adapters, resources, versioned codec). Backends ship separately: `@oimdb/persist-memory`, `-localstorage`, `-idb`, `-async-kv`, `-json` |
| `@oimdb/react` | React hooks for collections and selectors |
| `@oimdb/exodra` | [Exodra](https://exodra.org) adapter: OIMDB selectors/computeds → read-only `TExoBindable` (no React) |
| `@oimdb/async` | Async-aware reactive collection and index variants |
| `@oimdb/devtools` | Debug registry: name collections/indexes/computeds, inspect runtime state |
| `@oimdb/snapshot-manager` | Snapshot/restore collection state |
| `@oimdb/redux-adapter` | Bridge OIMDB collections into a Redux store |

## Core Concepts

### Event Queue

All reactive updates are batched. Mutations accumulate, then `queue.flush()` delivers all changes at once.

```ts
import { OIMEventQueue, OIMEventQueueSchedulerImmediate } from '@oimdb/core';

const queue = new OIMEventQueue({
    scheduler: new OIMEventQueueSchedulerImmediate(), // macrotask: setImmediate (Node), fallback MessageChannel / setTimeout(0) (browser)
    onError: (e) => reportToSentry(e),                // optional; see below
});
// or: OIMEventQueueSchedulerMicrotask (next microtask, before paint — lowest latency),
//     OIMEventQueueSchedulerAnimationFrame, OIMEventQueueSchedulerTimeout
// Async schedulers coalesce; call queue.flush() directly for sync delivery (e.g. tests).
// OIMEventQueueSchedulerSync (createSync()) flushes synchronously per write, NO batching —
//   debug/diagnostic only: swap in at the root to test if a bug is coalescing-related.
```

**Errors during flush.** If a task (subscriber / effect / computed) throws while the queue is flushing, the other tasks in that flush still run (each is isolated) and the queue's internal state is always restored — one bad task never wedges the queue. By default the error is then **raised, not swallowed**: it propagates out of `flush()` (thrown to the caller of a manual flush, or uncaught in async/scheduled mode). Pass `onError` to handle it instead (then it is NOT re-raised). Regardless of `onError`, a `EOIMEventQueueEventType.FLUSH_ERROR` event (payload `TOIMFlushError = { error }`) is emitted per failing task — the channel `@oimdb/devtools` `trackFlushErrors` / MCP use to surface failed flushes.

### Collections

`OIMCollection` — base CRUD store. `OIMReactiveCollection` — same + emits events on flush.

```ts
import { OIMReactiveCollection } from '@oimdb/core';

interface User { id: string; name: string; role: 'admin' | 'member'; }

const users = new OIMReactiveCollection<User, string>(queue, {
    selectPk: (u) => u.id,
});

users.upsertMany([
    { id: 'u1', name: 'Alice', role: 'admin' },
    { id: 'u2', name: 'Bob',   role: 'member' },
]);
users.upsertOne({ id: 'u1', name: 'Alice Smith', role: 'admin' }); // update
users.removeOne({ id: 'u2', name: 'Bob', role: 'member' });

users.getOneByPk('u1');   // → entity or undefined
users.getAll();            // → TEntity[]
users.getAllPks();          // → TPk[]
```

### Indexes

Indexes map keys to sets or arrays of PKs. Two storage shapes:
- **Set-based** — unordered, deduped (`OIMIndexManualSetBased`, `OIMReactiveIndexManualSetBased`)
- **Array-based** — ordered, with duplicates (`OIMIndexManualArrayBased`, `OIMReactiveIndexManualArrayBased`)

```ts
import { OIMReactiveIndexManualSetBased } from '@oimdb/core';

const byRole = new OIMReactiveIndexManualSetBased<'admin' | 'member', string>(queue);

byRole.setSlots('admin', [users.getSlotByPk('u1')!]);
byRole.getPksByKey('admin'); // → Set { 'u1' }

byRole.subscribeOnKey('admin', () => {
    console.log('admin set changed');
});
queue.flush(); // delivers subscription
```

**`subscribeOnKeys(keys, handler)` delivery is coalesced per flush:** the handler fires at most ONCE per flush no matter how many of the subscribed keys changed in it (the callback gets no key, so per-key fan-out would be pure waste). This holds across all reactive primitives — sync (collection / index / object, via `OIMCarrierKeyedEmitter`) and the `@oimdb/async` nodes (via `OIMUpdateEventEmitterAsync`) alike. `subscribeOnKey` (single key) is unchanged. Handler identity is preserved, so `unsubscribeFromKeys(keys, handler)` still removes a `subscribeOnKeys` subscription — and releases the coalescing exactly like the returned unsubscribe closure does.

**Coalescing is scoped to the subscription, not to the handler.** It applies only to handlers registered through a multi-key `subscribeOnKeys`. If the same function holds several *independent* `subscribeOnKey` subscriptions, it still gets one delivery per changed key — an unrelated multi-key subscription elsewhere on the same collection/index never changes that.

Membership writes are incremental (touch only the changed pks):
- `addPks(key, pks)` / `removePks(key, pks)` — **set-based**: O(1) per pk for both. **array-based**: `addPks` O(1), `removePks` O(bucket) (ordered, must scan).
- For frequently changing membership (e.g. a **virtual/windowed list** indexing the on-screen rows, adding/removing on scroll) prefer **set-based**.
- `setPks` / `addPks` resolve each pk → slot (O(1) lookup); if you already hold slots (`collection.upsertMany` returns them) use `setSlots` / `appendSlots` to skip the lookup.
- `getEntitiesByKey(key)` returns `(TEntity | undefined)[]` — positional holes for not-yet-loaded pks, aligned with `getPksByKey` (not dropped), so you can render a loading state.

### Global (keyless / whole-collection) indexes

When you need ONE index/ordered list over the **whole collection** ("all") there is no meaningful key. Use a **Global** index instead of inventing a phantom key like `'all'`. Same two shapes (array-based ordered / set-based unordered) and two modes (manual / derived), but keyless: `getPks()` / `getSlots()` / `getEntities()` take no key, and `subscribe(handler)` replaces `subscribeOnKey`. Internally a Global index holds ONE bucket with a single-carrier emitter (no key→carrier map / hashing), so it is strictly cheaper than a keyed index with one key.

Classes mirror the keyed ones with `Global` inserted: `OIMGlobalIndexManual{Array,Set}Based` (raw slots), `OIMReactiveGlobalIndexManual{Array,Set}Based`, `OIMReactiveCollectionGlobalIndexManual{Array,Set}Based` (pk writes), `OIMDerivedCollectionGlobalIndex{Array,Set}Based`.

```ts
// Manual, collection-bound (pk writes) — e.g. a server-provided page order
const list = indexFactory.arrayBasedGlobalIndex();
list.setPks(['u2', 'u1']);          // also addPks / removePks (no key)
list.getPks();                       // ['u2', 'u1']
list.subscribe(() => { /* one bucket changed */ });
queue.flush();

// Derived — auto-tracks the whole collection, ordered
const recent = indexFactory.derivedArrayGlobalIndex({ orderBy: (u) => u.createdAt });
recent.getEntities();                // (User | undefined)[] in order, kept in sync

// Derived set — whole-collection membership; `filter` narrows it
const active = indexFactory.derivedSetGlobalIndex({ filter: (u) => !u.archived });
```

- Derived options: `orderBy` / `compareEntities` (array only) for order, `filter: (e) => boolean` to include a subset (default: entity exists), `buildInitial` (default true).
- Selectors: `select.entitiesByArrayGlobalIndex(list)` / `select.entitiesBySetGlobalIndex(set)` → `(TEntity | undefined)[]` (no key).
- React: `useSelectEntitiesByGlobalIndex{Array,Set}Based(collection, index)`, `useSelectPksByGlobalIndex{Array,Set}Based(index)`, plus `…Signal` variants — all drop the `key` argument.

### Composite (key-path) indexes

When the key is a **combination of values** (e.g. `[userId, projectId, role]`) rather than one primitive, use a **composite** set-based index instead of concatenating a string key. Create it with `indexFactory.compositeSetIndex()`. The key is a `TOIMKeyPath` — an ordered, **arbitrary-length** tuple of primitive segments (`readonly (string | number)[]`). Every method that takes a `key` takes a path array instead; everything else (pk writes, slot resolution, reactivity, `getEntitiesByKey` holes) is identical to `setBasedIndex`.

```ts
const membersByScope = indexFactory.compositeSetIndex();
membersByScope.setPks(['u1', 'p1', 'admin'], ['m1', 'm2']); // also addPks / removePks
membersByScope.getPksByKey(['u1', 'p1', 'admin']);          // Set { 'm1', 'm2' }
membersByScope.getEntitiesByKey(['u1', 'p1', 'admin']);     // (Member | undefined)[]
membersByScope.subscribeOnKey(['u1', 'p1', 'admin'], () => {/* … */});
queue.flush();
```

- **Matched by content, not reference / string.** A freshly built `['u1','p1','admin']` resolves to the same bucket as the one written earlier — no need to reuse the array instance. Segments keep their own type (`1` ≠ `'1'`) and no separator can collide (`['a|b','c']` ≠ `['a','b|c']`), unlike a `"a|b|c"` string key.
- **Full path is the lookup unit.** O(arity) — effectively O(1) for a fixed arity — a lookup walks one native-`Map` level per segment. No partial/prefix queries (subscribe/lookup are by the whole path). Paths of different lengths coexist (`['a','b']` and `['a','b','c']` never collide).
- **No perf cost to primitive indexes.** It is a distinct opt-in index: `setBasedIndex` and all others keep their native-`Map` fast path untouched. The trie cost is paid only where you use a composite index.
- **Ordered variant:** `indexFactory.compositeArrayIndex()` — same key path, but buckets are ordered slot arrays (`getPksByKey` returns an array in write order). Use it when order matters per composite key (e.g. `[channelId, threadId]` messages).
- **Selectors:** `select.entitiesByCompositeSetIndexKey(index, path)` / `select.entitiesByCompositeArrayIndexKey(index, path)` → `(TEntity | undefined)[]`, tracking both index and entity changes.
- **React:** `useSelectEntitiesByCompositeIndexKey{Set,Array}Based(collection, index, path)` and `useSelectPksByCompositeIndexKey{Set,Array}Based(index, path)`. Unlike the primitive hooks (which stabilize the key by `===`), these stabilize the path **by content**, so a freshly built `['p1','admin']` on every render does not re-subscribe.
- New exports: `OIMReactiveCollectionIndexCompositeTrie{Set,Array}Based`, `OIMIndexStoreTrieDriven{Set,Array}Based` (inject via `indexOptions.store` for a custom key path store), `OIMKeyPathCarrierProvider`, `OIMTrieMap` (the generic N-level trie util), types `TOIMKeyPath` / `TOIMKey`. The keyed-emitter / index generics accept `TKey extends TOIMKey` (= `TOIMPk | TOIMKeyPath`) — a pure widening; primitive keys are unaffected.

### Composite PRIMARY key (collection keyed by a tuple)

Beyond composite index *keys*, a **collection's PK itself** can be a composite path. Pass a trie store: `new OIMReactiveCollection(queue, { selectPk: e => [e.userId, e.projectId], store: new OIMCollectionStoreTrieDriven() })`. Then `getOneByPk([1,10])`, `subscribeOnKey([1,10])`, `removeOneByPk([1,10])` all match by content; the store interns each logical PK to one canonical `slot.pk` reference so downstream native `Set<pk>` stays correct. Primitive-PK collections keep `OIMCollectionStoreMapDriven` (native `Map`) untouched — no regression.

- **Indexes work over a composite-PK collection.** `indexFactory.setBasedIndex()` (or `compositeSetIndex`) on such a collection indexes composite PKs: `byRole.setPks('admin', [[1,10],[2,10]])`, `getPksByKey`, `addPks`, `removePks([[2,10]])` all match PKs by content (the per-bucket pk→slot membership uses the collection's trie key domain).
- **Serialization boundaries.** `@oimdb/persist` (stores entities as an array, re-derives the PK via `selectPk` on hydrate) and `@oimdb/snapshot-manager` (stores the PK as a value) round-trip a composite PK with **no codec** — just pass the composite-PK collection. **`@oimdb/redux-adapter`** keys Redux state by string (`Record<pk, entity>`), so a composite PK needs an `IOIMPkCodec`: pass it to `createCollectionReducer(collection, child?, mapper?, pkCodec)` — one codec drives both the default mapper (encode: `entities` keyed by JSON-encoded PK, `ids` keep the raw tuple) AND child write-back / linked-index sync (decode: Redux string key → raw PK). `OIMPkCodecKeyPath` is the ready codec. (Or pass `mapper: createDefaultCollectionMapper(codec)` directly for a read-only projection.)
- New exports: `OIMCollectionStoreTrieDriven`, `OIMKeyDomainTrie` / `OIMKeyDomainNative` (`IOIMKeyDomain`), `OIMTrieSet`, `IOIMPkCodec` / `OIMPkCodecKeyPath`. The collection/index PK generics accept `TPk extends TOIMKey`.

### Ordered list command stream

For an ordered per-key list that emits **position-addressed commands** (insert / remove / move / set / reset) instead of a new array to diff — for imperative renderers that apply edits in place. `OIMCollectionOrderedListCommandStream` (pk writes, via `indexFactory.orderedList()`) or `OIMOrderedListCommandStream` (slot writes). Commands are not in the event payload — subscribe, then pull synchronously.

```ts
import { createOIMOrderedListMappedCommandStream } from '@oimdb/core';

stream.push('main', 'u1');           // append by pk; also insertAt/setAt/removeAt/removeRange/moveRange/set
stream.subscribeCommands('main', () => {
    for (const cmd of stream.consumeCommands('main')) {
        // { type:'insert', index, item } | { type:'remove', index, count? }
        // | { type:'move', from, to, count? } | { type:'set', index, item }
        // | { type:'reset', items }   — item is the entity slot; entity is item.item
    }
});
stream.getEntitiesByKey('main'); // (TEntity | undefined)[] — holes preserved
```

`count` defaults to 1 (read `count ?? 1`). A whole-list change collapses to a single `reset`. Reads: `getPksByKey` / `getSlotsByKey` / `getEntitiesByKey`.

**Mapping the list to your own elements** — `createOIMOrderedListMappedCommandStream(source, create)` projects element-wise: the same commands with `item` replaced by `create(slot)`'s result (a DOM node, view model, …). `create` is a plain function (no options object). Identity is positional — a `move` reuses the **same** mapped instance (never recreated); `create` runs on insert/set/reset/initial build. No teardown callback: the leaving element IS the `remove`/`set`/`reset` command the consumer applies against its own mirror, so cleanup belongs there. It needs no queue (rides the source's batching) and is itself an `IOIMOrderedListCommandSource`, so it consumes like the raw stream and chains via `.map(create)`. New exports: `IOIMOrderedListCommandSource`, `OIMOrderedListMappedCommandStream`, `createOIMOrderedListMappedCommandStream`.

```ts
const nodes = createOIMOrderedListMappedCommandStream(stream, (slot) => engine.makeNode(slot.item));
nodes.subscribeCommands('main', () => {
    for (const cmd of nodes.consumeCommands('main')) {
        // cmd.item is your node; tear it down on remove/set/reset from your own mirror
    }
});
nodes.getItemsByKey('main'); // current mapped elements — initial render
```

> Content updates (entity fields changed) are not list commands — they arrive via the collection's per-pk subscription. The stream carries structure only.

**Deriving commands from an index** — the stream above is written imperatively. To instead get commands from an index whose order is maintained automatically (`derivedArrayIndex`, or any reactive array-based index replaced via `setPks`), use `createOIMOrderedListCommandStreamDiffDriven(queue, index, opts?)` / `OIMOrderedListCommandStreamDiffDriven`. On each per-key index change it diffs the previous order against the new one and emits the `insert`/`move`/`remove` that transforms it — identity by pk (a reorder is a `move` of the same slot, never a recreate), delivered on `AFTER_FLUSH`. An order-preserving change emits nothing. `opts.resetThreshold` (default `0` = always diff): below that fraction of shared pks it emits one `reset` instead of many edits. Output is an `IOIMOrderedListCommandSource`, so `createOIMOrderedListMappedCommandStream` composes on top to carry your own nodes. New exports: `OIMOrderedListCommandStreamDiffDriven`, `createOIMOrderedListCommandStreamDiffDriven`, `TOIMOrderedListDiffOptions`, `diffOrderedListByPk` (pure diff), `OIMOrderedListCommandBuffer` (shared abstract base of both streams).

```ts
const cardsByDeck = cards.indexFactory.derivedArrayIndex((c) => c.deckId, { orderBy: (c) => c.position });
const stream = createOIMOrderedListCommandStreamDiffDriven(queue, cardsByDeck);
stream.subscribeCommands('deck1', () => engine.apply(stream.consumeCommands('deck1'))); // insert/move/remove
```
